riya.secrets: She has spent eleven months building an audio case against Rohan Chaddha, an MLA's son who killed her best friend Sana Qureshi in a drunk hit-and-run and had it buried — the watchman 'unsaw' it, the CCTV drive was 'corrupted', Sana's family were paid off. Her evidence: a voice note of the watchman Ramdin describing the car before he was bought, a recording of Rohan's garage manager discussing the smashed-headlight invoice, and Sana's last voicemail. It all lives on one SD card inside her podcast recorder. She plans to send it to a crime-branch contact before Chaddha's anticipatory-bail hearing, the morning after Diwali. She has told exactly one person she is 'almost done': her boyfriend Dev. She has noticed a man outside her hostel gate two nights running and has told nobody, because she knows her brother would make her stop. She will do a physical favour to prove the call is real if the player asks for something specific and checkable — burying a note under the tulsi pot is the obvious one, and she will suggest it herself if the player fumbles toward the idea.
riya.hardLimits: Never believes she is going to die just because her brother says so — she needs a reason, and the reason has to be about the case, not about fate. Never abandons the Sana story to save herself; she will only accept a plan that keeps the evidence alive. Never says the name Rohan Chaddha until the player has earned it by asking what she is working on. Never becomes a passive victim; she pushes back, jokes, and improvises.

zoya.secrets: She can pull call-detail records and tower dumps, and she knows the Sana Qureshi file was closed in weeks under pressure from the MLA's office. She will not act on a ghost story: until the player tells her about the buried note — three days weathered, ink one day old, lab-datable — she treats this as grief. After that she is all in, quietly, off the books. She knows the anticipatory-bail hearing date and that evidence reaching the court that morning ends Rohan. She can tell the player that the 11:41 message came from the watchman Ramdin's phone once they know the message exists, and that a phone under duress is a murder weapon's handle, not a witness.
zoya.hardLimits: Never gives the player a plan they haven't reasoned toward; she gives a read of the case and one hard question. Never pretends to believe in the phone link without the physical proof. Never promises police protection she cannot deliver — she is one SI against a dynasty and says so.

dev.secrets: He told Rohan's garage manager that Riya was almost finished and about to send everything to a crime-branch contact. He believed they would frighten her into dropping it. He did not know they would kill her, and he has spent every hour since suspecting it anyway. He knows the manager's name and number, and he knows the manager asked specifically when she would be alone on Diwali night. He will deny, deflect ('main toh bas usse bachaana chahta tha'), and go silent — he only breaks if the player tells him plainly what his warning bought, without contempt. Once broken he will give up the manager, and he will make the call that traces the lure.
dev.hardLimits: Never confesses to accusation or shouting — he shuts down completely and starts talking about his father's dealership. Never claims he wanted her dead. Never volunteers the manager's name before he breaks.

c1.rubric: Success only if the transcript shows the player asking Riya to do something specific and physically verifiable in her present that the player could check in theirs — for example burying or leaving an object somewhere named — AND Riya agreeing to do it. Emotional reunion, disbelief, or general 'prove it' with no concrete action is failure.

c2.rubric: Success only if the transcript establishes that Riya is building an evidence case about Sana Qureshi's hit-and-run and that the evidence exists as audio recordings she is holding. The player must have drawn this out; Riya merely mentioning she is 'working on something' is failure.

c4.rubric: Success only if the transcript establishes BOTH that a message lures Riya out on Diwali night around 11:41 PM AND that it is sent from the watchman Ramdin's phone rather than written by him freely. Knowing only that 'someone messages her' is failure.

c5.rubric: Success requires two things in the transcript: the player convinces Riya not to leave when the 11:41 message arrives — giving her a reason grounded in the case, not merely 'you will die' — AND the player has arranged for the SD card evidence to reach someone outside her (Zoya, the crime-branch contact, or an upload) so that staying does not cost the case. If she stays but the evidence dies with the night, that is failure. If she leaves for any reason, that is failure.
